title: Submission Hygiene Audit
text: A broker-by-broker audit of submission completeness found that BRO-W (West region) frequently supplies incomplete exposure detail at quote stage — approximately 55% of BRO-W submissions are missing exposure component breakdowns. Comparing bind rates, incomplete-exposure submissions convert to bind at only ~45% versus ~68% for complete submissions; those that do bind produce worse subsequent loss ratios. The audit recommends requiring structured exposure fields from BRO-W before quote release and is a significant factor in any submission-quality score.

title: UW Note Quality Review
text: A review of underwriting notes identified hedging phrasing in pricing notes as a meaningful leading indicator of subsequent under-pricing. Hedging phrases such as 'should be fine', 'best estimate subject to confirmation' and 'indicative at this stage' appear in roughly 35% of pricing notes attached to overridden 5437 risks. Hedging pricing notes — a modest but non-trivial signal — correlate with premium below model indication and with subsequent adverse development on the bound policy.

title: Override Discipline Memo
text: Downward risk-score overrides are heavily concentrated on class 5437, where 55% of submissions carry an override reducing the model score by 8-15 points. These overrides are a dominant driver of under-pricing and significantly elevate loss frequency over the next two quarters. The Override Discipline Memo is a primary reference for any underwriting quality assessment: the agent should weight risk_score_override heavily.

title: Site Inspection Findings
text: Site inspections that flagged an issue but were bound anyway produce ~40% more claims than clean binds. The flagged-inspection signal is a significant contributor to elevated loss frequency; the demo narrative around inspection_flag_ignored is grounded here. In a handful of cases the flag was waived because of a downstream risk-score override — Loss Control recommends treating unresolved flags as a binding gate.

title: Pricing Adequacy Brief
text: Binds on overridden 5437 risks are priced approximately 15% below the model indication while still carrying materially higher expected loss costs. Brief: pricing_inadequacy is a primary driver of negative margin contribution on the segment. The memo marks premium adequacy as the single largest margin lever for the segment.

title: FNOL Latency Briefing
text: First-Notice-of-Loss latency exceeds 14 days on roughly 45% of class 5437 claims. Late FNOL is a meaningful driver of elevated severity on the segment. Claims recommends a FNOL monitoring rule keyed to the class; the late_fnol signal is a moderate factor in any claims-quality score.

title: Reserving Discipline Memo
text: Initial reserves set below 60% of final settlement cost drive a high settlement-vs-reserve ratio (above 2.0) and show leakage averaging approximately 22% beyond the reserved amount. Approximately 35% of claims are under-reserved in this manner; reserve_adequacy is a major driver of leakage_pct and the primary signal in any settlement-quality assessment. This memo is the dominant reference for the reserve-adequacy driver.

title: Cycle-Time Impact Study
text: Days-to-settle above 180 compound leakage through additional ALAE and supplemental reserves. While only a modest portion of settlements exceed 180 days, settlement_slowness is a meaningful contributor to total leakage; the study recommends prioritising the long tail. Settlement slowness is a moderate signal — meaningful enough to cite, smaller than reserve adequacy.
